name: Armenian (Eastern)
variety: Standard Eastern Armenian as spoken in Yerevan, in the reformed orthography of Armenia
sources: Seyfarth, Scott, Dolatian, Hossep, Guekguezian, Peter, Kelly, Niamh & Toparlak, Tabita (2024). Armenian (Yerevan Eastern Armenian and Beirut Western Armenian). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 54(1): 445-478.
Seyfarth, Scott & Garellek, Marc (2018). Plosive voicing acoustics and voice quality in Yerevan Armenian. Journal of Phonetics 71: 425-450.
Hacopian, Narineh (2003). A three-way VOT contrast in final position: data from Armenian. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 33(1): 51-79.
Toparlak, Tabita (2019). Etudes phonétiques en arménien. Mémoire de master, Université Paris III Sorbonne Nouvelle. Formant values as published in Seyfarth et al. (2024).
Dum-Tragut, Jasmine (2009). Armenian: Modern Eastern Armenian. Amsterdam: John Benjamins.
Vaux, Bert (1998). The Phonology of Armenian. Oxford: Clarendon Press.

Skopeteas, Stavros (2021). Distinguishing tonal events within word-final stress: focus and question intonation in Eastern Armenian. Manuscript, University of Göttingen. Cited from Seyfarth et al. (2024).

Kelly, Niamh E. & Keshishian, Lara (2021). Voicing patterns in stops among heritage speakers of Western Armenian in Lebanon and the US. Nordic Journal of Linguistics 44: 103-129 (summary of Eastern Armenian voice onset times).

vowel_formants.speaker: adult male (mean of three male speakers from Yerevan, aged 21-40, words in sentences and in isolation)
vowel_formants.source: Toparlak 2019, as tabulated in Seyfarth et al. 2024, Table 2
vowel_formants.notes: Arrays are F1, F2, F3 in Hz, rounded to 10 Hz by the source. Female means (Table 1): i 340 2380 3170, e 500 2040 2880, ə 550 1660 2790, ɑ 680 1410 2690, o 450 1190 2680, u 350 1070 2690. The back vowels /ɑ o u/ are fronted by about 200 Hz after aspirated and voiced plosives.

contrasts: three-way laryngeal contrast in plosives and affricates: voiced, voiceless unaspirated, voiceless aspirated, kept in word-initial and word-final position
dental against postalveolar affricates, three of each
six vowels, schwa among them; no vowel length
/f/ is rare and found mainly in loanwords
allophony: the voiced plosives /b d ɡ/ are breathy voiced [b̤ d̤ ɡ̈] in Yerevan speech, with voicing through the closure and a breathy start of the following vowel, but usually without audible aspiration; about 15% of word-initial tokens have no closure voicing

the voiceless unaspirated plosives have the longest closure (123 ms word-initially against 109 ms voiced and 97 ms aspirated); some speakers add glottal constriction, and word-final tokens under emphasis may be ejective, but this is neither general nor required
the aspirated plosives and affricates have post-aspiration in onset and coda, and raise F0 at the start of a following vowel
in a number of words a written voiced plosive or affricate is pronounced voiceless aspirated, often after r: երգ [jeɾkʰ] 'song', մարդ [mɑɾtʰ] 'man', ձագ [dzɑkʰ] 'young animal'
regressive devoicing in obstruent clusters: the first obstruent is voiceless before a voiceless one; /v/ may devoice after a voiceless obstruent

the tap /ɾ/ is often spirantised in the coda, with frication around 4 kHz, and is a tap or approximant between vowels; the trill /r/ is often voiceless or spirantised in the coda and reduced to a tap word-initially
/ʁ/ varies between a fricative and an approximant; /χ ʁ/ vary between uvular and velar
/n/ takes the place of a following obstruent: [suŋk] 'mushroom'
/t d tʰ/ are dental, for some speakers laminal alveolar; /k/ may be backed towards [q]
/e/ is mid [e̞], /o/ is close enough to overlap with /u/ in F1, /ɑ/ is central to back
schwa is mid central; it is kept in careful speech and often dropped in colloquial connected speech
written word-initial ե is [je] and ո is [vo] in native words
phonotactics: written consonant clusters are broken by an unwritten schwa: գրել is [ɡəˈɾel], մկրատ is [məkˈɾɑt]; only /Cj/ onsets and a few loanword clusters have no schwa
word-initial sibilant plus stop may take a prothetic schwa ([əs]); in Yerevan this is variable and forms without it are now common
two-consonant codas with falling sonority need no schwa; final clusters with rising sonority take one: վագր [ˈvɑɡəɾ] 'tiger', փոքր [ˈpʰokʰəɾ] 'small'
stem-final /kʰ/ is added to any coda without schwa: պարտք [pɑɾtkʰ] 'debt'
nasal plus obstruent clusters are homorganic
vowel hiatus is repaired by an inserted [j] or by /u/ becoming [v]
in native words coda /j/ stands only after /ɑ/ and /u/

stress.rule: Stress falls on the last syllable unless its vowel is schwa, in which case it falls on the last full vowel; clitics are unstressed, and grammars report a secondary stress on the first syllable.
stress.cues: a pitch rise at the right edge of the word, which is a phrasal tone, and expansion of the vowel space; duration and F0 rise clearly only under focus (Seyfarth et al. 2024)

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: only schwa is reduced or dropped; full vowels keep their quality, but high vowels alternate with schwa or zero when derivation moves the stress

length.notes: No length contrast. Identical consonants meet across morpheme boundaries only.

voice_onset_time_ms.source: Seyfarth & Garellek 2018 (eight Yerevan speakers, word-initial plosives in a carrier phrase), as summarised by Kelly & Keshishian 2021; Hacopian 2003 for the ranges
voice_onset_time_ms.notes: The values are means for each series over all places of articulation, entered under the labials. Aspiration is about 75 ms for the aspirated series and about 15 ms for the unaspirated series. The voiced series has voicing through the whole closure, so its lead equals the closure duration (mean 109 ms). Hacopian (2003) found 66-92 ms for aspirated and 7-31 ms for unaspirated bilabials in three speakers.

intonation.declarative: each constituent before the nucleus ends in a rise (low then high at its right edge), the peaks step down from one constituent to the next, and the sentence ends with final lowering to a low boundary
intonation.yes_no_question: word order of a statement; a sharp rise on the stressed syllable of the verb or of the focused word, and a high final boundary
intonation.wh_question: rise on the question word, the rest of the sentence deaccented, low final boundary
intonation.continuation: high target at the right edge of each non-final constituent
intonation.accent_shape: rise to a high target on the final, stressed syllable of the word; under narrow focus a fall H+L that starts at the left edge of the stressed syllable
intonation.notes: After Skopeteas (2021) as reported by Seyfarth et al. (2024). Words after the focus are deaccented.

phonation: breathy voice on the voiced plosives and at the start of the vowel after them (first harmonic 2-3 dB louder than after the unaspirated series)
optional glottal constriction of the voiceless unaspirated plosives and affricates; ejective release is occasional, mostly word-final and emphatic

problems: ղ /ʁ/ is sent to the phoneme r" (uvular trill, IPA ʀ); the uvular fricative that ph_armenian defines as Q is not used by the rules.
ր /ɾ/ is the base phoneme r, an approximant of the English type [ɹ] before vowels; ռ is the trill R.
Written voiced plosives and affricates that are pronounced aspirated are read as voiced: երգ gives [jerɡ], մարդ gives [mard], արջ gives [ardʒ].
No devoicing in obstruent clusters: աղջիկ gives [aʀdʒik] for [ɑχtʃʰik].
No schwa before a word-final ղ after a consonant: աստղ gives [astʀ] for [ɑstəʁ].
A prothetic schwa is always put before initial sibilant plus stop (սպիտակ gives [əspitˈak]); in Yerevan speech it is variable and often absent.
The voiced plosives are plain voiced and the unaspirated ones have no longer closure; the breathy and constricted voice qualities are not modelled.
The default intonation tunes are used: no rise at the right edge of non-final words.
good: the three series of plosives and affricates are kept apart: voiced, unaspirated (p, t, k, ts, tS) and aspirated (p#, t#, k#, ts#, tS#)
stress is final and never falls on schwa, with a secondary stress on the first syllable of longer words
the unwritten schwa is inserted in initial clusters (գրել, մկրատ, նկար) and before final r, n, m after a consonant (փոքր, վագր)
word-initial ե is [je] and ո is [vo]
the trill ռ and the rhotic ր are different phonemes

notes: Eastern Armenian has no phonemic ejectives. The voiceless unaspirated series is sometimes described as glottalised or ejective; instrumental work finds some glottal constriction for some speakers and only occasional ejective release (Seyfarth & Garellek 2018; Seyfarth et al. 2024).
